questions.prompt: Match each element to its electron arrangement.
What is the electron arrangement of magnesium (12 electrons)?
questions.explain: 2 in the first shell, 8 in the second, 2 in the third.

questions.prompt: How many valence (outer shell) electrons does phosphorus (15) have?

questions.explain: Lose or gain the fewest electrons to reach a full outer shell; full shells have valency 0.

questions.prompt: Why do noble gases have a valency of zero?
options: Their outer shells are already full
questions.explain: A full outer shell is stable, so they don't need to lose, gain or share electrons.

questions.prompt: Element X has the arrangement 2, 8, 6. Which statement is correct?
options: It is in group 6 and period 2
It is in group 16 and period 3, with valency 2
questions.explain: 3 shells → period 3; 6 outer electrons → group 16; needs 2 more → valency 2. It's sulfur.

questions.text: The first shell holds up to ___ electrons. The second shell holds up to ___ electrons.

questions.prompt: What is the valency of nitrogen (atomic number 7)?
questions.hint: Arrange 7 electrons, then work out how many it needs to GAIN.

questions.prompt: Explain why sodium and potassium have similar chemical properties.
questions.modelAnswer: Sodium (2, 8, 1) and potassium (2, 8, 8, 1) both have 1 electron in their outer shell. Chemical properties depend on the outer electrons, so they both lose one electron easily and react in similar ways (e.g. both react vigorously with water).
rubric: Chemical properties depend on outer electrons
An example of a similar property/reaction
questions.explain: Same number of outer electrons → same group → similar properties.
